sourceEvidence: The prior generated notice board had two posts, one thick backing block, four frame rails and LOD0 corner fasteners, but no clear weather cover, dry display cavity, perimeter seal, hinge/latch hardware or actual posted notices. At benchmark distance this risked reading as a generic framed slab rather than a manufactured neighborhood information case.

The shared park-furniture microdetail pass rewrites generated meshes to metre-space planar UV0. The first notice-sheet implementation assumed legacy 0..1 UVs, which would crop/stretch the unique paper textures after that rewrite unless per-material tiling was normalized from physical sheet dimensions.

The first acrylic material used smoothness 0.89 (roughness 0.11). That was inside the case-specific acrylic range but below the existing scene-wide furniture roughness hard floor of 0.12, so the final pipeline normalizes it to smoothness 0.86 / roughness 0.14 rather than weakening either gate.

The first acrylic setup declared Standard shader mode 3 but used Fade-style SrcAlpha blending/ALPHABLEND. Unity documents Transparent mode as the appropriate mode for realistic clear plastic/glass because reflections and highlights remain visible; final prepared-scene normalization enforces premultiplied Transparent semantics instead.
criticalDefectRisk: materially impossible or visually weak transparent-specular response

materials.paper: rough dielectric with five deterministic print textures; printed ink remains texture detail
materials.clearCover: transparent dielectric acrylic; final smoothness 0.86 / roughness 0.14, metallic 0, premultiplied Standard Transparent mode so real scene reflections/highlights are retained

implementation.printedTextureMapping: After shared metric-UV rewrite, each notice material uses _MainTex scale = inverse physical sheet width/height and offset=(0.5,0.5), Clamp + mipmaps + sRGB. Five distinct paper textures persist through all four LOD tiers.
implementation.lod: Case/cover/gasket/three hinges/latch and five-notice occupancy persist through LOD0/1/2/3; only ten 7 mm pin heads are LOD0-only. All generated case renderers are created before the explicit furniture LOD rebind and formal completed-scene validation rejects escape from the assigned tier.

referenceResearch.use: Built-in Standard shader Transparent mode is the appropriate mode for realistic clear plastic/glass because material alpha can be transparent while reflections and lighting highlights remain visible.
Confirms TextureImporterCompression.CompressedHQ is supported in Unity 6 and selects a high-quality platform-appropriate compression format.

qaEnforcement: Machine-readable notice-board contract records components, dimensions/thickness, materials/finish, mounting sequence, interfaces/gaps/seals, orientation/exposure, cause-based aging, geometry-vs-material allocation, four-level LOD policy and zero automatic visual credit.

Scene construction QA rejects missing case parts, incorrect paper/backing seating, insufficient paper/cover air gap, incorrect cover clearance, hood/frame gap, wrong hinge count, wrong notice count, generated colliders, stock primitive meshes, metallic paper/acrylic and missing notice textures.
Printed-UV QA rejects physical sheet tiling drift, repeated/cropped sheet mapping, non-clamped/non-mipmapped/non-sRGB notice imports, missing UV0 and post-microdetail acrylic blend/roughness drift.

Benchmark save builds the case before LOD rebind, then runs metric microdetail, printed-UV/acrylic normalization and completed-scene validation. Formal native-4K review repeatedly calls the existing furniture LOD validator, which now also validates the completed notice-board case and printed mapping before/after capture stages.
No source-side PASS clears a rendered critical defect; native 3840x2160 and 100% crops remain mandatory.

implementationReadiness.reason: The remaining seven readiness points are reserved for actual Unity compile/runtime evidence. Source-side construction reasoning, dimensional math and QA cannot satisfy them.

expectedVisualScoreImpact.geometryConstruction: Potential deduction recovery because a benchmark-visible framed slab is now a physically layered weatherproof display case with depth, gasket, hinges/latch, hood and seated paper; no point is assumed until pixels prove it.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.materialPbr: Potential improvement because painted steel, exposed metal, board/paper, EPDM and clear acrylic now use separate physical material classes and the acrylic uses reflection-preserving Transparent semantics; grazing evidence is mandatory.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.textureMicrodetail: Potential improvement because five unique notice textures are mapped once per physical sheet after metre-UV conversion instead of being cropped/stretched/repeated; actual aliasing/legibility remains render-dependent.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.periodAuthenticity: Potential deduction recovery because a passive posted-notice weather case reads more plausibly as ordinary circa-2000 neighborhood infrastructure than a blank generic panel; exact historical-product credit is not claimed.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.temporalLod: Potential stability improvement because case/cover/notice occupancy persists through all four tiers and only sub-pixel pins disappear after LOD0; actual cross-fade/pop must be judged from temporal evidence.
